article.title: The Note in the Stone
article.summary: Comparative archaeoacoustic evidence across six Neolithic & Iron Age chambers (95–120 Hz standing waves) and Maeshowe's 2 Hz Helmholtz resonance vs Newgrange's permeable silence.

sites.name: Maeshowe

passage_dims_m.hes_notes: 10 m visitor page / ~15 m formal statement; outer rebuilt 1861

sites.masonry: Tightly dressed Devonian flagstones ('effectively solid stone'); 4 corner buttress standing stones; 3 raised single-slab side cells; clay-sealed mound.

helmholtz_measured.status: Confirmed empirically (Watson & Keating 1998): only Neolithic site with measured Helmholtz resonance

key_features: Square 4.7 × 4.7 × 4.5 m plan stacks third axial modes (3,0,0) and (0,3,0) onto 109.8 Hz
38 ideal-box modes below 130 Hz; 13 within 95–120 Hz
Recessed blocking stone leaves narrow gap to passage ceiling for acoustic coupling

sites.name: Newgrange
sites.location: Brú na Bóinne, Co. Meath, Ireland
sites.masonry: Rounded water-rolled Carboniferous greywacke orthostats with permeable gaps; 18-course corbelled vault with rainwater grooves cut in roof slabs; quartz facade.

helmholtz_measured.status: Predicted 1–2 Hz by Watson & Keating (2001), but measured NO response due to permeable stone joints & roof drains

key_features: ~12 fixed antinode/node pairs (λ/2 ≈ 1.56 m) along the 19 m passage like a wind instrument
Open Roof-Box above entrance doorway acts as Winter Solstice light slot and potential acoustic mouthpiece
West recess corbel bears carved zigzag lines matching nodal loop count (Jahn et al. 1996 observation)

sites.name: Loughcrew Cairn L
sites.location: Slieve na Calliagh, Co. Meath, Ireland
sites.masonry: Radial upright partition orthostats dividing the chamber into 7 stone compartments around an eccentric standing pillar stone.
key_features: Jahn et al. (1996) speculated builders may have positioned sector stones to sharpen resonance
Toggleable interior partition orthostats in our 3D model & live FDTD comparison (Test #2)

sites.name: Loughcrew Cairn I
sites.location: Slieve na Calliagh, Co. Meath, Ireland
sites.masonry: Seven-compartment radial orthostat chamber similar in plan to Cairn L.
key_features: Closely matches Cairn L's compartmented resonance despite smaller outer cairn diameter

sites.name: Wayland's Smithy
sites.masonry: Large sarsen megaliths forming a cruciform gallery with opposing ~1.5 × 1.5 m East and West transept side chambers.
key_features: Opposing ~1.5 × 1.5 m side chambers naturally fit ~110 Hz half-wavelength (λ/2 ≈ 1.56 m)
Asymmetry between East & West stone clearances shifts the primary standing wave from 112 Hz to 95 Hz

sites.name: Chûn Quoit
sites.masonry: Four inward-leaning granite orthostats enclosing a compact ~1.5 m cube under a 3.3 m domed mushroom granite capstone.
sites.measured_band_label: 110 Hz measured (113 Hz Jahn 1.5 m box model)
key_features: Smallest chamber in the 1994 survey (~1.5 m across), demonstrating exact λ/2 ≈ 1.56 m cavity scaling
Jahn et al.'s simple 1.5 m box model predicted 113 Hz vs 110 Hz measured

sites.name: Carn Euny (Fogou Beehive)
sites.masonry: Circular dry-stone corbelled granite beehive chamber (~4.6 m diameter) joined to a curved subterranean stone creep passage.
key_features: Iron Age subterranean corbelled chamber ~2,800 years younger than Newgrange yet still inside 95–120 Hz

voice_benchmarks.source: Sydney Voice Lab v4.0 (2025), citing Leung, Oates, Papp & Chan, Journal of Voice 36(3) (2022)

eeg_study.citation: Cook, I. A., Pajot, S. K., & Leuchter, A. F. (2008), Time and Mind 1(1), 95–104
eeg_study.findings: Relative drop in left temporal brain activity and shift in prefrontal cortex balance from left to right at 110 Hz compared with 90, 100, 120, and 130 Hz.
eeg_study.caveats: Authors labeled results 'pilot findings'. Watson & Was (2021) noted 'no robust scientific evidence that single frequencies can trigger specific physiological effects' and pointed out significant methodological inconsistencies.

palaeolithic_caves.citation: Fazenda, B., Scarre, C., Till, R., et al. (2017), JASA 142(3), 1332–1349
palaeolithic_caves.region: Northern Spain (images up to ~40,000 years old)
palaeolithic_caves.finding: Lines and dots were statistically more likely to occur where low-frequency rock acoustics resonated ('a statistically weak but tenable hypothesis').

etruscan_tombs.citation: Ortoleva, J., & Forte, M. (Sep 2026), The Conversation
etruscan_tombs.finding: Two painted Etruscan tombs exhibited deliberately engineered long reverberation designed to affect living ritual participants.
